title: Foundations of GenIR
extended_summary:
This chapter/paper discusses foundational concepts for generative information retrieval (GenIR) and how modern generative AI models change information access systems. It argues that generative models create two major new paradigms for IA: information generation, where models directly produce tailored content for user needs, and information synthesis, where models integrate external information to provide grounded responses.

The paper does not study a K-12 educational intervention or any human participants. Instead, it surveys and organizes the technical foundations of generative models, including Transformer architectures, scaling laws, training stages such as pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and RLHF, as well as prompt optimization and multimodal applications. It then turns to information synthesis, especially retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), modular RAG, retrieval planning, generative retrieval, and domain-specific modeling.

Its main conclusion is that generative AI can substantially enhance information access, but the most reliable path for many applications is information synthesis rather than unconstrained generation because of hallucination and external-knowledge requirements. The chapter positions future work around better retrieval-generation integration, improved prompt and retrieval planning, and more controllable, explainable systems. It is a conceptual and technical overview rather than an empirical study.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual chapter/review on generative AI and information access, not an empirical study in K-12 education. It does not present a clear methodology, sample, or evaluative design for student outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No student, classroom, or school-level outcome is measured, and no effect sizes are reported. The paper is theoretical/background-oriented rather than evidence of impact for science inquiry supports in K-12.
